challenge.better_approach: Considered: (a) a module-level memo with a TTL, rejected because a time bound is a guess and a later crossing in the same process would read a stale listing; (b) passing the listing down as an argument, rejected because proof_coverage.lacks and crossings_for sit three calls deep and would each grow a parameter; (c) caching in proof_coverage only, rejected because has_crossings and buildme_crossing are reached from other sieves too. A scope opened by the one caller that knows the tree is still (inspect) is the smallest change.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That no sieve writes a new history.json during inspect(); measured by reading: inspect() is a read-only shake. If one did, its own journal would be missed until the next inspect(), which is the cost of the pin.
challenge.prior_art: 8ad6's one-shake ruling (inspect() docstring, 2026-08-06) is the same reasoning applied to sieves; _BREACH_CACHE, _CENSUS_DIRS and _IOU_CACHE in inspector.py are per-inspect caches cleared at entry. 50987 cured a similar cost by reading standing seals. No intention in intentions-congruency-lab names the journal walk.
challenge.real_collision: None. crossings._index's docstring says the reader IS the event and the invalidation is a stat; the pin keeps the stat invalidation for bytes and pins only the listing, inside a scope a caller opens deliberately.

answers.falsifier: (1) over one whole-tree inspect(), Path.rglob('history.json') is called at most once per root; (2) outside the scope journals() walks afresh each call, so a history.json created between two calls is seen by the second; (3) inside the scope a journal whose bytes change is re-parsed (the _index stat key still invalidates). WRONG INTENT if the whole-tree inspect() wall time drops by less than 60 s, since then the walk was not the cost.
answers.from_idea: none, because this is a measured cost, not an idea: the cProfile at /tmp/claude-1000/-home-akien-dev-src-cairn/0b2e196e-7177-4140-8585-e9f2200689b4/scratchpad/prof_pct.out (2026-11-22, akiendelllinux) shows crossings._index -> journals() rglob run 2041 times inside one proof_covers_the_ticket scan, ruled into a sibling ticket of 9cfc by the orchestrator
answers.how: crossings.py gains a scope (a context manager) that pins journals()'s listing per roots for its duration; inspect() opens that scope around its shake and post-shake scans. _index's stat-keyed parse cache is unchanged, so a journal written mid-sweep is still re-read; only the directory walk is pinned. A proof counts rglob calls over one whole-tree inspect() (1) and records its wall time.
answers.traces_to: Law 1 (the resolver is spent on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled): the tree does not change within one inspect(), so re-walking it 2041 times re-derives a settled listing; and 9cfc's 600 s bound on test_inspector, which this cost is breaking.
answers.what: One build_inspector inspect() walks the two roots for history.json once, not once per crossings lookup.

bullets.text: proof_covers_the_ticket spends 164 of 253 s (cProfile) re-walking both repos for history.json, 2041 times in one sweep, because _index's cache key needs a fresh rglob each call.
The PROVED re-judge (1000 tickets, 246 s) is a second, separate redundancy; it is a sibling ticket after this one.

title: One build_inspector inspect() walks the two roots for history.json once, not once per crossings lookup.
